long_biography.plain_text:
Bill Duker began in law, working at Cravath before establishing his own New York firm. That background became relevant when he joined Ideal Ventures, the investment firm that formed Amici, an Albany company providing document-management and electronic-discovery services to law firms.

Amici turned a specialised legal workflow into a scalable technology business. Xerox agreed to acquire the company for $174 million in 2006. Duker then continued as a private investor. His later activity has included financing a major commercial lawsuit arising from alleged manipulation of Venezuelan oil auctions by major commodity-trading houses.

uncertainties.detail: BOAT International's owner log directly pairs Bill Duker with the saved current yacht Danneskjold, while Forbes and El País connect the same American software businessman to Sybaris, later Badis I. The two vessel histories, name, nationality and business identity converge strongly. Vessel facts are nevertheless excluded from the biographies and classifications.

Bill Duker is the father. His son is William West Duker, generally called West. Forbes records that they worked together in software, but public sources identify West separately in Rational Enterprise leadership. No founder, managing-director, education or other corporate fact belonging to West has been assigned to Bill.

The Albany Business Review says Duker was part of Ideal Ventures, which formed Amici, while current reporting calls him an Amici co-founder and Bloomberg Law calls Amici one of his companies. The biographies use the conservative wording 'helped form Amici'; the Enterprise software tag records a venture-principal relationship rather than inventing a precise operating title.

Amici was acquired in 2006, so Technology is treated as the wealth-creation industry rather than a proven current operating sector. Bloomberg's 2023 account and current 2026 reporting identify Duker as an investor, supporting Finance & Investments and Investor for the present relationship. A complete personal asset schedule is not public.

No family transfer or inherited asset is evidenced.

Government and legal sources use William F. Duker, and the career history connects that name to the Bill Duker in the owner record. Because only an initial is established rather than a full middle name, no middle-name proposal is made. Weak biographical sites give a 1954 birth year and more precise dates, but no sufficiently strong source was found, so all birth fields remain blank.

No LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website or company website is proposed. Forbes articles are reporting pages, not a personal profile.

Enterprise software is the single minimum useful active tag because Amici's software-and-services business was a defining wealth event. Lawyer is omitted because it is a former profession rather than a current practiced role in this record; Venture capital lacks sufficiently specific evidence of a sustained specialist mandate; Competitive sailing is omitted because the evidence does not clearly separate a defining competitive identity from private recreational ownership.
